intro: Look up, and you will see a night sky made of tiles. You are in the Karatay Museum of Tiles, in Konya province, a Seljuk madrasa built in 1251. Its dome is tiled in blue and black like the night, and beneath it are displayed the figured tiles taken from the Kubadabad palace.
history: The madrasa was built in 1251 for the Seljuk emir Celâleddin Karatay, and since the middle of the twentieth century it has served as a museum of tiles. The blue, black and turquoise of its dome compose a night sky, reflected in the pool below. The heart of the collection, though, is the figured tilework taken from the Kubadabad palace on the shore of Lake Beyşehir.
highlights: As you wander, begin with the Dome tiles above you, then turn to the Tiles from Kubadabad. Don't miss the Portal, and look for the Muqarnas squinches.
facts: Did you know? The Kubadabad tiles carry hunting birds, sirens and double-headed eagles, the richest surviving figural decoration of Anatolian Seljuk art. And the dome of the madrasa was designed as a night sky reflected in the pool below, its blue and black tiles making the stars.
outro: This brings our tour of the Karatay Museum of Tiles to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these colours keep shining for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
